auth_google.s:
Google OAuth at `/google` — ~/AGENTS.md is explicit that the callback URL is always `/google`, never `/google/callback`. Both legs live in one route handler, exactly like `~/i/x2/src/routes/google/+server.ts` (read it before writing this).

INSTALL: `pnpm add arctic`.

CREATE `src/routes/google/+server.ts`:
- Client factory: `new Google(await get_secret(env.GOOGLE_ID), await get_secret(env.GOOGLE_SECRET), new URL('/google', origin).toString())`.
- START leg (no `code` query param): `generateState()` + `generateCodeVerifier()`, store both in short-lived httpOnly cookies (`oauth_state`, `oauth_verifier`, `maxAge: 600`), redirect 302 to `g.createAuthorizationURL(state, verifier, ['openid', 'email', 'profile'])`.
- CALLBACK leg (`code` present): compare the returned `state` against the `oauth_state` cookie and 400 `bad_oauth` on mismatch — this is the CSRF guard, do not skip it. `validateAuthorizationCode(code, verifier)`, then `GET https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo` with the access token. No email on the profile -> 400.
- ACCOUNT RESOLUTION, in this order: (a) a user with this `g` (google sub) exists -> log into it; (b) a user with this `e` exists -> attach `g` to it and log in (same human, they signed up with a password first); (c) `locals.user?.dv` is true -> upgrade that device row in place (`patch_user` with `g`, `e`, `n`, `pic`, `dv: 0`) so the guest keeps their summaries; (d) otherwise create a new user. Mint the session, delete both oauth cookies, redirect 302 to `/`.
- Top of the handler: if `locals.user && !locals.user.dv`, redirect straight to `/` — an already-logged-in user has no business re-running the flow.

provider_keys.s:
'add any provider under the sun, even with a custom base url' — implemented as ONE provider type, OpenAI-compatible, because that shape covers openai, groq, openrouter, deepseek, together, mistral, xai, local ollama, and both anthropic and google via their compatibility endpoints. One code path, one dependency, no per-vendor adapters to maintain.

INSTALL: `pnpm add ai @ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (the versions x2 runs and that are current: `ai@^7`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@^3`).

CREATE `src/lib/server/crypto.ts` — AES-GCM at rest for the api keys:
```ts
export async function enc(master: string, plain: string): Promise<string> {
	const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
	const ct = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, await mk(master), new TextEncoder().encode(plain));
	return `${b64u(iv)}.${b64u(new Uint8Array(ct))}`;
}
export async function dec(master: string, blob: string): Promise<string> { ... }
```
`mk` derives a 256-bit AES key from `MASTER_KEY` with SHA-256 and imports it for `['encrypt','decrypt']`. Store `iv.ciphertext` base64url in `pv.k`. Decrypt ONLY at call time, inside the request that needs it — never on a list endpoint, never into a page load.

CREATE `src/lib/server/pv.ts`: `list_pv(db, uid)` (returns `{ id, n, b, m }` — the key is NEVER in this shape), `add_pv(db, master, uid, { n, b, k, m })`, `del_pv(db, uid, id)` (the `uid` in the WHERE clause is the authorization check — do not delete by id alone), `pv_key(db, master, uid, id)` (the only decrypting function), and:
```ts
export function model_of(base: string, key: string, id: string) {
	return createOpenAICompatible({ name: 'p', baseURL: base.replace(/\/$/, ''), apiKey: key }).chatModel(id);
}
```

ROUTES:
- `GET /api/pv` -> `{ p: [...] }` from `list_pv`.
- `POST /api/pv` body `{ n, b, k, m }` -> validate `b` parses as an https URL, `add_pv`, return `{ id }`. Calls `ensure_session` first so a guest can save a key without signing up.
- `DELETE /api/pv/[id]`.
- `GET /api/pv/[id]/models` -> server-side `fetch(`${b}/models`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${key}` } })`, map to `{ m: string[] }` sorted. This is why there is no hardcoded model list anywhere in the codebase — every OpenAI-compatible provider serves `/models`. On non-200 or unparseable JSON return `{ m: [] }` and let the UI fall back to a free-text model input; a provider with a broken `/models` must not block using it.

UI `src/routes/settings/+page.svelte`: list saved providers (label, base url, masked key as `••••` + last 4), an 'add provider' form (label / base url / api key / optional default model), and a model `<select>` populated from `/api/pv/[id]/models` with a text input fallback. Placeholder text should show a real example base url (`https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`) so the shape is obvious. `use:ctrl_enter` on the form. All lowercase.

extract_input.s:
Turn whatever the user pasted into `{ ty, text | media_url, title }`. Pure classification plus one webpage fetcher. No LLM, no network cost beyond a single GET.

CREATE `src/lib/server/extract.ts`:
```ts
export type Input = { ty: 'w' | 'x' | 'v' | 'a'; t: string; text?: string; media?: string; src?: string };
export function classify(raw: string): 'url' | 'text' { ... }
```
`classify`: trim; treat as a url only when it starts `http://` or `https://` AND has no whitespace AND `new URL()` parses. Everything else is pasted text — including a 200-page essay, which is the whole point of letting people paste into the same box.

`extract_page(url)`: `fetch` with a normal desktop `user-agent`. Branch on the response `content-type`:
- `text/html` -> pull the title from `<title>` and the body text with **HTMLRewriter**, which is native to Workers — no `@mozilla/readability` (needs a DOM), no `cheerio`, no parser dependency at all. Drop the contents of `script`, `style`, `noscript`, `nav`, `footer`, `header`, `aside`, `form`; collect text from everything else; collapse runs of whitespace; cap at 400k chars. Returns `ty: 'w'`.
- `audio/*` or `video/*` -> return `ty` `'a'`/`'v'` with `media` = the url, no body read. NEVER pull media bytes through the Worker; the transcription provider fetches the url itself.
- `application/pdf` or anything else -> throw a 415 with a message naming what was received. A silent wrong answer is worse than a clear refusal.
Also branch BEFORE fetching on a known-media file extension in the path (`.mp3 .m4a .wav .ogg .opus .flac .mp4 .webm .mov .mkv`) so obvious media never gets a wasted body read.

`is_media_host(url)`: true for youtube.com / youtu.be / vimeo.com / soundcloud.com / open.spotify.com / twitter.com / x.com / tiktok.com / instagram.com. These are player PAGES, not media files — HTML scraping returns navigation chrome, not content. For them: try captions (next step); if that fails and `COBALT_URL` is set, ask cobalt to resolve a direct media url; if it is not set, throw a typed error `needs_extension` that the UI renders as 'install the extension to summarize this'. This is the honest behaviour: a Cloudflare datacenter IP cannot reliably pull YouTube, and pretending otherwise produces a feature that breaks in a week.

`cobalt_resolve(base, url)`: `POST base` with `{ url }` and `accept: application/json`, read `.url` from a `redirect`/`tunnel` status. ~20 lines, entirely skipped when `COBALT_URL` is blank.

captions.s:
Free path first: if a video already has a transcript, we pay nothing. This is the single largest cost saving in the app and must be tried before any transcription.

CREATE `src/lib/server/captions.ts` — `get_captions(url): Promise<string | null>`:
- YouTube: fetch the watch page, regex out `ytInitialPlayerResponse`, walk `captions.playerCaptionsTracklistRenderer.captionTracks`, prefer a track whose `languageCode` starts with `en` and that is not `kind: 'asr'`, else the first track, then fetch its `baseUrl` with `&fmt=json3` and join the `events[].segs[].utf8` fragments. Strip the timing, keep the words.
- Vimeo: `https://player.vimeo.com/video/{id}/config` -> `request.text_tracks[0].url`, fetch the WebVTT, strip cue numbers and timestamps.
- Anything else: return null.
Return null — never throw — on ANY failure (blocked, no captions, layout changed, network error). Captions are an optimisation; a null just means 'fall through to transcription'.

BE HONEST IN THE CODE COMMENT-FREE WAY: this path is expected to fail from a Cloudflare datacenter IP a large fraction of the time, because YouTube gates server-origin requests. It costs one cheap GET to try, it is free when it works, and the extension path (which runs on the user's own residential IP, inside a logged-in browser, on the page itself) is the reliable version of the same thing. Do not add retries, proxies, or PO-token machinery — that is a maintenance treadmill for a fallback that already has a better sibling.

Cache the result: `s.tr` in R2 under `cap/{sha256(url)}` so a second summarize of the same video (different model or length) never refetches.

transcribe.s:
Speech to text when captions came back null. Uses the SAME saved provider record and the SAME api key as the summary — no second credential, no extra sdk package.

CREATE `src/lib/server/stt.ts`:
```ts
export async function transcribe(base: string, key: string, model: string, media: string): Promise<string>
```
Implementation: `GET media` (streaming), then `POST ${base}/audio/transcriptions` as `multipart/form-data` with fields `file`, `model`, `response_format: 'text'`, `authorization: Bearer ${key}`. Return the text.

WHY A RAW FETCH AND NOT `experimental_transcribe`: the AI SDK's transcription models live in separate per-vendor packages (`@ai-sdk/groq`, `@ai-sdk/deepgram`, ...), which would reintroduce exactly the per-vendor dependency sprawl that `provider_keys` deleted. `/audio/transcriptions` is the same de-facto standard endpoint the chat path already assumes, so one 15-line fetch reuses the saved provider verbatim. Default model id `whisper-large-v3-turbo` (groq, roughly 2 kobo-scale cents per audio-hour), overridable per provider via a `HOUSE_STT_MODEL`-style field.

BYTES: prefer handing the provider a url when it accepts one, but the OpenAI-compatible endpoint takes a file part, so stream the response body straight into the FormData `Blob` without buffering the whole file into a variable. Cap at 25 MB — above that, refuse with a typed `too_large` error rather than burning Worker CPU. The extension path uploads already-extracted audio, so this cap bites rarely.

STORE the transcript in R2 at `tr/{summary_id}` and put that key in `s.tr`. This is what makes 're-summarize with a different model' and 'change the length' cost zero speech-to-text on the second run — the reason the transcript is kept at all.

summarize_stream.s:
The core route. Ties classify -> captions -> transcribe -> llm together and streams the answer back.

CREATE `src/lib/server/prompt.ts`:
```ts
export const LEN = { s: '3 sentences', m: '5 to 8 bullet points', l: 'a thorough section-by-section breakdown' } as const;
export function build_prompt(ty: string, len: 's' | 'm' | 'l', title: string) { ... }
```
Output contract, identical for every input type so the downloaded .md is always the same shape: an H1 with the title, a `**tl;dr**` line, a `## key points` bulleted list sized by `len`, and — only for `ty` `v`/`a` and only when the transcript carried timestamps — a `## chapters` list of `- 12:34 — what happens`. Instruct the model to output GitHub-flavoured markdown and nothing else: no preamble, no 'here is your summary', no closing offer to help.

CREATE `src/routes/api/sum/+server.ts` (POST, body `{ i, ln, pv, md }` = input / length / provider id / model id).

THE HANDLER ORDER IS FIXED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. Later steps (`summary_cache`, `paid_tier_model`) add code INTO these numbered slots; they never re-open the ordering question, and nothing may be inserted ahead of slot 2. Slots 2a and 4a/4b are empty in this step and filled later — leave them as the seams they are:
1. `ensure_session(event)`.
2. `classify(i)`; for a url, `extract_page`/`is_media_host` from `$lib/server/extract`. Compute `src` (the normalised url, or null).
2a. [`summary_cache` fills this] cache lookup on `src`. A hit returns before ANY grant, hold, extraction or model call — a cached answer is never charged.
3. For media: `get_captions(url)` first; on null, `transcribe(...)`.
4. Guard the size: if the text exceeds 300k chars, map-reduce — split on paragraph boundaries into ~120k-char chunks, summarize each with the same model, then summarize the concatenated chunk summaries. 300k, not 700k: `extract_page` already caps a webpage at 400k, so a 700k threshold would make this branch unreachable for every input except a pasted essay. Set `n_calls = chunks + 1` and carry it forward — slot 4b prices the hold off it, and a map-reduce charged as a single call is a straight cost leak.
4a. [`paid_tier_model` fills this] `maybe_grant`.
4b. [`paid_tier_model` fills this] estimate and `deduct` the hold, multiplied by `n_calls`.
5. `streamText({ model: model_of(base, key, md), system: build_prompt(...), prompt: text })`, return `result.toTextStreamResponse()`.
6. In `onFinish`, write the row: `insert into s (...)` with `id = new_id()`, `t` = extracted or model-generated title, `h` = the cache hash from the next step, `tr` = R2 key or null. Wrap the write in `platform.ctx.waitUntil(...)` so the response is not held open by the insert.
7. Errors: `needs_extension` -> 422 with `{ e: 'needs_extension' }`; no provider saved -> 400 `{ e: 'no_provider' }`; provider 401 -> 402-style `{ e: 'bad_key' }`. The UI maps each to a specific sentence — never a generic 'something went wrong'.

summary_cache.s:
Same link, same model, same length -> return the stored summary and charge nothing. Roughly 15 lines for the biggest cost saving in the product.

CREATE `src/lib/server/cache.ts`. There is no `sha256_hex` in this repo yet — define it locally in this file (`crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', ...)` -> hex string, the same shape `uuid_from` in `db.ts` already uses); do NOT add a dependency and do NOT touch `crypto.ts`:
```ts
export async function cache_key(src: string | null, md: string, ln: string): Promise<string | null> {
	if (!src) return null;
	let u: URL;
	try { u = new URL(src); } catch { return null; }
	if (u.protocol !== 'https:' && u.protocol !== 'http:') return null;
	return sha256_hex(`${u.origin}${u.pathname}${u.search}|${md}|${ln}`);
}
```
PRIVACY RULE, do not weaken it: `h` is null for pasted text and for uploads, so those are NEVER shared between accounts. A cache hit is only ever served for a public http(s) URL — content anyone could have fetched themselves. Normalising through `new URL` strips the fragment and keeps query strings (a `?v=` or `?t=` genuinely identifies different media).

IN `src/routes/api/sum/+server.ts`. The previous step's file has no slot comments in it (this repo forbids comments in code), so place by position, not by marker:

1. Compute `src` FIRST. credits_d1.s:
The credit system, following ~/i/x2 and ~/i/e4 (kobo as the unit, 5400/day free grant, deduct-then-reconcile) but WITHOUT their Durable Object.

WHY NO DO: x2 needs `ws/src/credit_account.ts` because Qdrant cannot do a conditional write, so it borrows the DO's input-gate serialization to make read-modify-write atomic. D1 does not have that problem — a single SQLite UPDATE statement is atomic on its own:
```sql
update u set bal = bal - ?1 where id = ?2 and bal >= ?1
```
`meta.changes === 1` means the deduction happened; `0` means insufficient funds. No lost update is possible, no CAS loop, no second worker, no service binding, no DO migration. Do not reintroduce a Durable Object here.

CREATE `src/lib/server/credits.ts`:
- `DAILY_GRANT = 5400` (kobo), `RATE = 1.08` (the markup, matching e4's `TOKEN_RATE`), `DAY_MS = 86_400_000`.
- `maybe_grant(db, uid)`: `update u set bal = bal + 5400, lg = ?now where id = ?uid and lg < ?now - DAY_MS and dv = 0`. The `dv = 0` is the abuse guard — device-only accounts get no grant, because clearing a cookie mints a fresh device user and would otherwise be an infinite free tier. Guests must bring their own key. Log a `ce` row when it fires.
- `deduct(db, uid, amt)`: the conditional update above; returns `{ ok, bal }`; writes a `ce` row with `k:'deduct'` on success.
- `refund(db, uid, amt, ref)`: `update u set bal = bal + ?`; `ce` row `k:'refund'`.
- `add_credit(db, uid, amt, ref)`: the `ce` insert and the balance update go in ONE `db.batch([...])` — D1 runs a batch as a single implicit transaction, so either both land or neither does. `ce.ref` is UNIQUE, so a duplicate Paystack webhook fails the insert, which rolls the whole batch back and skips the balance update; the unique index is the idempotency guard, no separate `mark_processed` lookup like x2 needs. Do NOT write these as two sequential statements with the insert first: a worker that dies between them leaves the user paid, uncredited, and permanently un-retryable, because the surviving `ce.ref` row blocks both the webhook retry and the `/settings?reference=` reconcile that `paystack_credits` depends on. Both call sites lean on that batch being atomic.
- `history(db, uid)`: last 100 `ce` rows.

paystack_credits.s:
Buying credits, following `~/i/x2/src/lib/server/paystack.ts` (read it first — same env shape, same kobo unit, same test/live key switch).

CREATE `src/lib/server/paystack.ts`: `PaystackEnv` of `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY_TEST | PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY_LIVE | PAYSTACK_TEST | PAYSTACK_BASE_URL` (all `SecretVal`, all read through `get_secret`); `get_secret_key(env)` picks test vs live off the truthiness of `PAYSTACK_TEST`; `paystack_init(env, email, amount_kobo, reference, callback_url, metadata)` -> POST `/transaction/initialize`; `paystack_verify(env, reference)` -> GET `/transaction/verify/{ref}`.

`POST /api/credits/purchase` body `{ a }` (kobo): require a session, reject under 10_000 kobo (₦100 — Paystack's practical floor), `reference = new_id()`, email falls back to `{uid}@tldr.local` when the account has none, `callback_url` = `{origin}/settings`, metadata `{ uid }`. Returns Paystack's `{ authorization_url, access_code, reference }` straight through.

`POST /api/webhooks/paystack`: verify the `x-paystack-signature` header — HMAC-SHA512 of the RAW body with the secret key — and 401 on mismatch. Read the raw text BEFORE parsing JSON; parsing first and re-serialising changes the bytes and breaks the signature. On `charge.success`, call `add_credit(db, metadata.uid, data.amount, data.reference)`. Always return 200 to Paystack once the signature is valid, even for events we ignore, so they stop retrying.

Also verify on the callback leg (`/settings?reference=`) with `paystack_verify` — webhooks can be delayed and a user staring at an unchanged balance is the worst moment in the product. Both paths funnel through `add_credit`, and `ce.ref`'s unique index makes the double-call harmless. That is exactly why the guard lives in the schema.

UI in `/settings`: current balance in naira (`bal / 100`), quick-buy buttons (₦500 / ₦1000 / ₦5000), and the credit history list from `history()`.

paid_tier_model.s:
Let people who have not added a key just pay. BYOK stays completely free and untouched — it never enters this code path.

DECISION THAT KEEPS THIS SMALL: the paid tier runs ONE house model that we choose (`HOUSE_BASE_URL` / `HOUSE_KEY` / `HOUSE_MODEL` / `HOUSE_STT_MODEL` from the secrets store). Because there is exactly one model with one known price, cost is `tokens x KOBO_PER_1K x RATE` — no per-model pricing table to maintain, no vendor price change silently making us lose money on a model we forgot about. BYOK users keep picking any model they like; that is what the provider UI is for.

CREATE `src/lib/server/house.ts`: `house_model(env)` builds the `createOpenAICompatible` chat model from the secrets; `KOBO_PER_1K_IN`, `KOBO_PER_1K_OUT`, `KOBO_PER_AUDIO_MIN` as constants next to it; `cost_kobo(usage)` = `ceil((in/1000*IN + out/1000*OUT) * RATE)`.

IN `/api/sum`, when the request carries no `pv` — filling slots 4a and 4b that `summarize_stream` left, NOT at the top of the handler; the cache lookup in slot 2a stays ahead of both, so a cache hit neither grants nor charges:
1. (slot 4a) `maybe_grant(db, uid)`.
2. (slot 4b) Estimate a hold: `ceil(chars/4/1000 * KOBO_PER_1K_IN) + expected_out_kobo`, plus `minutes * KOBO_PER_AUDIO_MIN` when transcription will run — then multiply by the `n_calls` computed in slot 4, so a map-reduce over 6 chunks holds for 6 calls and not for one. `deduct` that hold.
3. Not ok -> return 402 `{ e: 'insufficient_credits', bal }`. The UI shows the balance and the buy buttons inline — never a dead end.
4. Run the stream. In `onFinish`, compute the real cost from `usage` and `refund(db, uid, hold - real)` when the hold overshot (it usually will). If the stream throws, refund the whole hold. Hold-then-reconcile is x2's pattern and it is the right one: a mid-stream abandon cannot leave the user charged for tokens that were never produced.
5. `dv:1` guests get no grant and no house model — a 400 `{ e: 'no_provider' }` pointing at settings. Stated plainly in the empty state: bring a key, or sign in for the free daily credits.

ext_manifest_menus.s:
The extension, in the site's own repo under `extension/`. Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no bundler — it is a few hundred lines and a build step would be pure ceremony.

CREATE `extension/manifest.json`:
```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "tldr",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "summarize any video, audio, page, or text",
  "permissions": ["contextMenus", "storage", "activeTab", "scripting"],
  "host_permissions": ["https://tldr.apexlinks.org/*", "<all_urls>"],
  "background": { "service_worker": "bg.js", "type": "module" },
  "content_scripts": [{ "matches": ["<all_urls>"], "js": ["content.js"], "run_at": "document_idle" }],
  "action": { "default_popup": "popup.html" },
  "icons": { "128": "icon.png" }
}
```
`<all_urls>` host permission is what makes the extension the reliable media layer: it fetches from the page's own origin on the user's residential IP with their cookies, so none of the datacenter-IP blocking that defeats server-side extraction applies.

CREATE `extension/bg.js` — on `runtime.onInstalled`, register four context menus:
- `sum_media`, contexts `['video', 'audio']` -> title `summarize this`
- `sum_page`, contexts `['page']` -> `summarize this page`
- `sum_sel`, contexts `['selection']` -> `summarize selection`
- `sum_link`, contexts `['link']` -> `summarize this link`
`onClicked` sends `{ k: menuItemId, info }` to the tab's content script via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`, awaits `{ i, t }` back (input text/url + title), then POSTs to `${SITE}/api/sum` with the stored bearer token and opens `${SITE}/s/{id}` in a new tab.

CREATE `extension/lib.js` with the pure logic so it is unit-testable from vitest (import it directly in a node test — no chrome globals in these functions): `pick_input(k, info, page)` mapping a menu id + `info` payload to `{ i, ty }`; `site_url(path)`; `slug(title)`.

CREATE `extension/icon.png` (a simple 128px mark in the accent colour) and add `"ext:zip": "cd extension && zip -r ../tldr-extension.zip ."` to package.json scripts.

ext_grab.s:
The content script — the part that makes the extension worth installing. It extracts what the server provably cannot.

CREATE `extension/content.js`, listening for `chrome.runtime.onMessage` and replying `{ i, t }`:
- MEDIA: for a `sum_media` click, `info.srcUrl` is often a `blob:` url that is useless off-page. Resolve properly: find the `<video>`/`<audio>` element under the click, read `currentSrc`, and if that is a blob, fall back to the site-specific path below. Never send a `blob:` url to the server — it cannot resolve it.
- YOUTUBE: read the caption track list from the page's own `ytInitialPlayerResponse` (available as a global in-page, reachable by injecting a tiny script tag into `document` and reading it back through a `postMessage`, because content scripts run in an isolated world). Fetch the `json3` caption url from the page context, join the segments, and send the TEXT — not the media. This is free, instant, needs no transcription at all, and works because the request originates from the user's logged-in browser on their home IP.
- PAGE: `document.title` plus text extracted by walking the DOM and skipping `script/style/nav/footer/header/aside/noscript`, collapsing whitespace, capped at 400k chars. Same rules as the server's HTMLRewriter path so both produce comparable input.
- SELECTION: `info.selectionText` verbatim.
Put every one of these in `extension/lib.js` as pure functions taking a document/object argument (`text_from_doc(doc)`, `captions_from_player(player_response, fetcher)`, `resolve_media(el)`), and keep `content.js` as thin glue. Pure functions are the only part worth testing and the only part likely to break.

NOTE ON THE TEST FILENAME: these fixtures need a real `document`, so they go in `src/lib/__tests__/ext_dom.svelte.test.ts`. The `.svelte.test.ts` suffix is what routes a file to the `client` (browser/chromium) vitest project — it does not mean the file renders a component. ext_popup_auth.s:
The popup: 'everything the site has, even login', with exactly one UI codebase.

CREATE `src/routes/e/+page.svelte` — the same components as `/`, laid out for a 400x600 popup: the textarea, the length/provider/model row, the streaming summary, and the recent list collapsed to five rows. Reuse the components from `home_ui`; do NOT fork them. If a piece of `/` is not extractable as a component yet, extract it now and let both routes import it — one implementation, two layouts.

CREATE `extension/popup.html` — a full-bleed `<iframe src="https://tldr.apexlinks.org/e">` and nothing else.

AUTH ACROSS THE IFRAME — the one genuinely tricky bit. The site's session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, so it is NOT sent inside a `chrome-extension://` iframe (that is a cross-site context). Rather than weaken the cookie to `SameSite=None`, carry a token:
1. `POST /api/auth/token` (session required) mints a 90-day signed token with the same `encode_session` HMAC and returns `{ t }`.
2. `popup.js` reads `chrome.storage.local['t']` and sets the iframe src to `/e#t={token}` when it has one.
3. `/e` reads `location.hash`, posts the token to `/api/auth/adopt` which verifies it and sets a normal first-party session cookie inside the iframe's own origin, then strips the hash via `replaceState`.
4. When there is no token, `/e` renders the same login card as `/login`; on success it `window.parent.postMessage({ t }, '*')` and `popup.js` stores it in `chrome.storage.local`. Validate the message origin against the site origin before storing — an `'*'` target is fine outbound, but never trust an inbound message without checking `event.origin`.
This keeps `SameSite=Lax` intact everywhere and gives the extension a durable login. The token is bearer-equivalent, so `/api/auth/token` must require an existing session and the token must be revocable by bumping a per-user version later if that is ever needed.

`extension/bg.js` uses the same stored token as its `authorization: Bearer` header for the context-menu POSTs, so menus work whether or not the popup was ever opened.

ship.s:
Create the real Cloudflare resources, ship it, and verify it live in a browser.

RESOURCES (run these, then paste the ids into `wrangler.jsonc` replacing PLACEHOLDER):
```
wrangler d1 create tldr
wrangler d1 migrations apply tldr --remote
wrangler r2 bucket create tldr
```

SECRETS — declare in `wrangler.jsonc` under `secrets_store_secrets: [{ binding, store_id, secret_name }]` and create each with `wrangler secrets-store secret create <store_id> --name KEY --scopes workers --remote`: `SECRET`, `MASTER_KEY`, `GOOGLE_ID`, `GOOGLE_SECRET`, `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY_TEST`, `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY_LIVE`, `HOUSE_KEY`. Non-secret config (`HOUSE_BASE_URL`, `HOUSE_MODEL`, `HOUSE_STT_MODEL`, `PAYSTACK_TEST`, `COBALT_URL`) goes under `[vars]`. Remote Secrets Store values are NOT readable in local dev — for `wrangler dev` create the same names WITHOUT `--remote`, and keep plain vars in `.env`.

GOOGLE CONSOLE: authorized redirect URI is `https://tldr.apexlinks.org/google` — exactly `/google`, per ~/AGENTS.md.

PAYSTACK: webhook url `https://tldr.apexlinks.org/api/webhooks/paystack`.

DEPLOY: `pnpm build && wrangler deploy`. If `pnpm install` fails in Cloudflare Workers Builds with 'packages field missing or empty', confirm `pnpm-workspace.yaml` still has `packages: ['.']` beside `allowBuilds` — it was added during scaffolding, do not let a regeneration drop it. If any deployment error mentions wrangler types, confirm `build` is still bare `vite build`.

DOMAIN: add the `tldr.apexlinks.org` custom domain to the worker.
